extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and advanced students in analytical geometry, algebra, and classical geometry (mid- to advanced-level readers)
extracted.subtask_description: Derivations, definitions and formulae for analytical geometry in three dimensions referred to oblique axes (directing/projecting coefficients, relations among cosines, distances, perpendiculars), plus related papers on symmetric functions, cubic solution method, and tetrahedron propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angles of ordination and cosines of ordination (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The angles which the axes make with each other will be called the angles of ordination, and the cosines of these angles the cosines of ordination" (notation f,g,h for cosines between axes). Also definition of the coefficient of cubature T = {1 — f^2 — g^2 — h^2 + 2fgh}^{1/2} and formulae to compute T from given cosines/angles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines terminology used throughout: cosines of ordination, projecting coefficients, directing cosines, coefficient of cubature; supplies equivalent formulae for T, including a product-of-sines form when angles of ordination are known. (Original wording and formulae given in text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations to a straight line (Prop. I)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let (a,B,y) be a fixed point and (x,y,z) a variable point on a straight line; if r projects on axes with constant ratios l,m,n to r, then the equations of the straight line are (x−a)/l = (y−B)/m = (z−y)/n. The quantities l,m,n are called the projecting coefficients of the straight line; the cosines of the directing angles (u,v,w) are the directing cosines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains geometric meaning: l,m,n are projections of a displacement on axes drawn parallel to coordinate planes; directing angles are those made by a parallel through the origin. Establishes parametric/projective form used throughout subsequent propositions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equations of a straight line through two given points (Prop. II)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two points (a1,y1,z1) and (a2,y2,z2), the straight line through them can be written in the ratio form (x−a1)/(a2−a1) = (y−y1)/(y2−y1) = (z−z1)/(z2−z1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derives by imposing that the generic point on the line satisfies both parametric equations; presents the familiar two-point form adapted to oblique-axis notation and indicates division to obtain required equations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition for intersection of two straight lines and point of intersection (Prop. III)
rubrics_metrics.description: For two lines given by their projecting-coefficient parametric forms (x=a+lr, y=B+mr, z=C+nr) and (x=a'+l'r', y=B'+m'r', z=C'+n'r'), elimination leads to a condition (explicit multilinear equation ((2m'n − m'n') (a−a') + ... ) = 0) that the lines intersect; solving the intermediate linear system gives the parameter r (or r') and hence the coordinates of intersection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the elimination steps (equations (7),(8) in text) and prescribes solving for parameters r and r' from linear relations; includes the explicit combined condition (equation (8)) to test intersection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance between two points in oblique axes (Prop. IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: If r is the vector between two points, with directing cosines u,v,w, then r^2 = (Δx)^2 + (Δy)^2 + (Δz)^2 + 2f(Δy)(Δz) + 2g(Δz)(Δx) + 2h(Δx)(Δy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derives by projecting broken line on axes and using orthogonal projections; presents the full quadratic expression including cross-terms involving the cosines of ordination f,g,h (formula (11)). Useful for computing lengths referenced to oblique axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation among projecting coefficients of a straight line (Prop. V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Projecting coefficients l,m,n of any straight line satisfy l^2 + m^2 + n^2 + 2fmn + 2gnl + 2hlm = 1 (equation (12)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtained by expressing r^2 both as square sum of coordinate differences and in terms of projections; this is the normalization relation tying projecting coefficients to the geometry of oblique axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Given equations to a straight line, find projecting coefficients (Prop. VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: From a line written in the form (x−a)/A = (y−B)/B' = (z−C)/C' (equations (13)) one can set l = W/A, m = W/B', n = W/C' and determine W by substituting into the projecting-coefficient relation to obtain an equation for W (equation (15)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: express projecting coefficients proportional to given direction numbers with an unknown scale W, substitute into relation (12) to solve for W (possibly multivalued), then recover l,m,n.

rubrics_metrics.name: Given projecting coefficients, find directing cosines (Prop. VII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directing cosines u,v,w of a line can be obtained from projecting coefficients l,m,n by formulae u = (l + f m + g n)/W', v = (g l + m + h n)/W', w = (h l + g m + n)/W' (equations (16),(17) — schematic form), where W' normalizes the vector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows how to eliminate coordinate differences and use projection relations to get closed-form expressions for directing cosines in terms of projecting coefficients and cosines of ordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Given directing cosines, determine projecting coefficients (Prop. VIII)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solving the linear system relating directing cosines and projecting coefficients yields explicit expressions for l,m,n in terms of u,v,w and f,g,h (equations (18)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides inversion formulae (explicit determinants/combinations) to go from direction cosines to projecting coefficients; useful when direction (angles) are known and one needs the projection ratios on oblique axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation among directing cosines (Prop. IX)
rubrics_metrics.description: Directing cosines u,v,w satisfy a quadratic relation analogous to the projecting-coefficient relation: u^2 + v^2 + w^2 + 2(gh−f)uv + 2(fh−g)vw + 2(fg−h)wu = 1 (equation (19)) — an identity expressing compatibility with the oblique-axis geometry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by eliminating projecting coefficients from their relations to directing cosines; provides a consistency check on any purported triple of directing cosines relative to given ordination cosines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angles axes make with normals to coordinate planes (Prop. X)
rubrics_metrics.description: If normals to the coordinate planes yz,xz,xy are taken (unit normals in axes directions), the cosines that the axes make with these normals are obtained by substituting unit vectors (1,0,0),(0,1,0),(0,0,1) into the directing-cosine relations (19) and simplifying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives method and specific substitutions; notes normals are taken on same side as positive axes, so resulting cosines are positive. Provides explicit expressions in the text for these cosines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angle which a straight line makes with normals to coordinate planes (Prop. XI)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a line with projecting coefficients l,m,n and directing cosines u,v,w, the cosines (A,M,N in text) with normals are given via projection: e.g. cosine with normal to yz is l·u (schematic); formulas are given in text (equation (41) and surrounding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derives by projecting broken lines on normals and dividing by r; gives explicit formulae expressing these cosines in terms of projecting coefficients and directing cosines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Angle of inclination between two straight lines (Prop. XII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If two lines have directing cosines (u1,v1,w1) and (u2,v2,w2), then cos θ = u1u2 + v1v2 + w1w2 (equation (22)), and eliminating either directing cosines or projecting coefficients gives expanded formulae for cos θ (equation (23)) and for sin^2 θ (equation (25)), both expressed in terms of projecting coefficients and the cosines of ordination f,g,h.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text supplies both compact dot-product form (in directing cosines) and detailed expanded algebraic forms in projecting coefficients that account for oblique-axis cross-terms; includes alternative forms when lines are given in different parametric representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition that two straight lines be perpendicular (multiple equivalent forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Perpendicularity (cos θ = 0) can be expressed in several equivalent algebraic forms: (i) u1u2 + v1v2 + w1w2 = 0 (simple form); (ii) in projecting coefficients a1l + a2m + ... = 0 (equation (31)); (iii) expanded polynomial forms in f,g,h and projecting coefficients (equations (32)–(36)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multiple algebraic tests; the text gives both succinct vector forms and expanded scalar identities — pick whichever is most convenient for computation in oblique axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for two straight lines to be parallel (Prop. XIV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two lines are parallel iff their projecting coefficients are proportional (l/l' = m/m' = n/n') or if corresponding direction numbers are proportional (equations (38),(39) in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes that Gregory's earlier expression is more complicated and shows how the simpler proportionality conditions follow from (16). Practical test: check ratios of projecting coefficients or direction numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length of perpendicular from a given point to a given straight line (Prop. XV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given point P(a,B,C) and a line with projecting coefficients l,m,n through Q, the perpendicular distance r is determined by projecting coordinate differences on the line: r = l(x−a) + m(y−B) + n(z−C) (equation (41)), and r is found explicitly by substitution into the quadratic expression (42) (full formula with f,g,h cross-terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives method: compute projection of PQ on line using projecting coefficients; full expression (42) yields the required perpendicular; also shows how to find foot coordinates from parameter value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perpendicular distance between two straight lines not in same plane (skew lines) (Prop. XVI)
rubrics_metrics.description: For skew lines (3) and (4), the shortest connecting perpendicular has projecting coefficients l',m',n' satisfying linear relations derived from the two lines (system NU + w m' + v' n' = 0, etc.). The perpendicular distance r' equals the projection N(a−a') + e(B−B') + o'(y−y') (equation (46)) and can be computed by substitution and reduction to known forms involving projecting coefficients and cosines of ordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: solve linear system to find directing cosines of perpendicular, then obtain projecting coefficients (via (18)), substitute into (46) to compute distance; text gives explicit combined formula after reduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Properties of symmetric functions: 'critical functions' and term cancellation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the theory of symmetric functions (Jerrard, Cockle discussion), certain constructed combinations (e.g. a = n p_{n} − (n−1) p_{n−1} p_1, etc.) are shown to be free of specified elementary symmetric sums (P, QP, etc.) — termed 'critical functions' — so particular terms disappear from these expressions by algebraic identities (see development around equations (3)–(4) and the subsequent deductions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains method of showing that particular symmetric-function combinations eliminate certain lower-degree elementary symmetric functions by combinatorial coefficient comparisons; references Jerrard's results and gives algebraic steps to identify which terms vanish.

rubrics_metrics.name: New method of resolving a complete cubic without removing the second term
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitution and decomposition approach is presented for solving a general cubic x^3 + a x^2 + b x + c = 0 without first depressing the cubic (removing the x^2 term). The method sets x = m + y + z with constraints leading to three algebraic relations; solving two quadratics for y and z yields m from a simple relation and then x. Worked examples illustrate the procedure and special simplified formulae for reduced forms are given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives explicit system of equations linking m,y,z (equations (1)–(10) in text), step-by-step elimination strategy, and worked numeric examples; claims the method avoids the usual preliminary transformation required for Cardan's method and is applicable to all cubic forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations among inscribed and escribed sphere radii of a tetrahedron (Prop. I & II)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a tetrahedron with face areas A1..A4, inscribed sphere radius r, escribed radii r1..r4 (each touches one face and the other three produced), perpendiculars p1..p4 from opposite vertices, volume V and surface S, identities such as r(A1 + A2 + A3 + A4) = 3V and r_i(−A_i + sum of other A_j) = 3V lead to algebraic relations among r, r_i, p_i, A_i, V and S (see equations (a)–(e) in text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derives radii expressions by decomposing the solid into pyramids from the in-/ex-sphere centers; shows how to combine reciprocals and form symmetric relations among perpendiculars and radii; presents many consequent neat algebraic identities (tables and compact relations in the text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Radius of circumscribing sphere of a tetrahedron (Prop. III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given tetrahedron with opposite-edge rectangles (products) denoted and half-sum 7, and volume V, the radius R of the circumscribing sphere is given by an explicit symmetric algebraic formula in the edge-lengths (text presents a multi-term polynomial expression and a compact form involving products (7−7_i) in denominator with V^2 etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derives via perpendiculars from face-circle centers and spherical trigonometry; gives both full expanded polynomial form and an alternate expression in terms of rectangles of opposite edges and volume for computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Area of opposite face from a given solid angle and edges (Prop. IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given solid angle at vertex D with incident edges a,b,c and dihedral angles at edges (d),(e),(f), the area A1 of the opposite face is A1 = A2 + A3 + A4 − 2(A2A3 cos d + A2A4 cos e + A3A4 cos f) (formula in text); if one dihedral is right-angled, simplifications occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents method: express side-squared quantities for triangle formed by edges in terms of given edge lengths and cosines of contained angles, substitute into Heron-like formula to get face area; gives simplified special-case expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distances from an angular point to centres of inscribed and escribed circles of opposite face (Prop. V)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit algebraic expressions are derived for distances from a vertex to the incenter and excenters of the opposite face, expressed in terms of side-lengths and area-related quantities (long rational expressions are provided in the text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural derivation using earlier cosine formulae; long reductions lead to final compact algebraic quotients for those distances — useful for advanced tetrahedral geometry computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sum-of-squares identity for distances of in/excentres from a point (Prop. VI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The sum of the squares of the distances of the inscribed and escribed circles of a plane triangle from a point in space equals four times the square of the distance of the circumscribing circle plus twelve times the square of its radius; special cases (e.g. point on circumcircle) yield known relations like p + p' + ... = 12R^2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derived by adding previously obtained squared-distance formulae and simplifying; provides a compact global identity tying several geometric centers and radii.
